# The result of a fold of maxima of one limb: the maximum, or NaN

Kernel `norm_finish_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The result of a fold of maxima from its final state, the largest magnitude $m$ and the mask $\mathit{ok}$ that no element was a NaN: $m$ when $\mathit{ok}$ is true and it is finite, with the flag $\mathit{flag}$ true; otherwise a NaN and the flag false (the canonical NaN of [When something is not finite](../developer/design/milestone2.md#sum-dot-axpy-convolution)):

$$r = m \ \text{when } \mathit{ok} \text{ is true and } m \text{ is finite}, \qquad r = \mathrm{NaN} \text{ otherwise}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own.

## Requires

- $m$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $\mathit{ok}$ is a mask, true or false.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{flag}$ is true exactly when $\mathit{ok}$ is true and $m$ is finite.
- When it is, $r = m$.
- Otherwise $r$ is a NaN.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/norm_finish_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/norm_finish_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`fold_finish_1`](fold_finish_1.md).

```
# The finish of norm_upper_1 (milestone2.md, "When something is not finite"): the largest magnitude
# when no element was a NaN (the mask ok) and it is finite, with the flag true; otherwise the
# canonical NaN and the flag false. An infinite element made m infinite.

t         = select(ok, m, const nan)
(r, flag) = fold_finish_1(t)
```
